sentence: This project studies how interactions between microbes decide whether a newcomer can join an existing community of nasal bacteria.
This project studies how grasses use low and high temperatures to decide when to flower, and which genes are involved.
This project sets up an instrument that separates, measures and identifies small and large molecules in many kinds of samples.
This project builds a mathematical framework that explains when changing training data helps or hurts machine learning models.
This project uses machine learning to look for solutions to problems with sustainable and resilient urban infrastructure.
This project studies how machine learning algorithms can keep personal data private and stay computationally efficient without losing accuracy.
This project builds computer software that helps people design folded structures and makes sure the designs fold successfully.
This project builds self-powered detector arrays from metal halide perovskites that can pick up very weak optical signals.
This project brings nanoengineering research on sustainable energy, clean water and health technologies into science classrooms.
This project studies how giant transposons move genes between fungal species and what conditions affect how often this happens.
This project studies how farming practices meant to help with climate change affect soil, farmer livelihoods and climate resilience.
This project studies how a fungus invades bat skin cells and tests a vaccine and a drug that block the infection.
This project develops antibodies that use two parts of the immune system to attack acute myeloid leukemia cells.
This project studies which chemicals in male spider bodies help females make better offspring when they eat the males.
This project tests whether signals in wastewater can show how much air pollution people in underserved communities are exposed to.
This project builds a self-driving laboratory where AI agents, robots and simulations work together to make advanced electronic and quantum materials.
This project builds a 3D chip with artificial neurons and artificial synapses that processes sensor signals and drives mechanical motion.
This project studies how algae, bacteria and fungi in freshwater biofilms are linked to what they do and to peatland carbon dioxide emissions.
